shows.name: Amityville Candycorn
shows.synopsis:
Randy is devastated after a fight with his girlfriend Sandy, who harbors a deep-seated trauma regarding candy corn. Determined to change her mind, he concocts an occult homemade batch in his kitchen using esoteric ingredients and a cauldron.

A supernatural storm triggers a portal to a distorted psychedelic dimension ruled by sentient corn entities. Encountering whimsical candy natives and the omnipotent Big Corn, Randy is tasked with becoming an emissary of confectionery love.

Randy is returned to the mortal realm, only to discover he has been physically transformed into a life-sized, immobile candy corn cone. Unable to resume normal life, he asks his roommate Mike to cast him adrift on a local lake as an offering to Halloween.

Camera style: Low-fi VHS camcorder footage with analog video synthesizer color distortion and feedback effects.

shows.name: BUTTFACE FACTORY
shows.synopsis: Welcome to an utterly absurd animated comedy where the world is literally turned upside down—and inside out. In this universe, everyone’s face is a giant, expressive pair of buttocks. It’s a cheeky, satirical cartoon that takes "talking out of your ass" to hilarious new literal heights.

shows.name: Center Core Nevermore
shows.synopsis:
In a surreal retro-futuristic metropolis, an unassuming woman completes her evening subway commute amid advertisements for bizarre consumer oddities. Upon returning to her apartment building, she is confronted in the hallway by a melting, disfigured humanoid.

The creature politely apologizes for its repellent form, explaining that it has crawled there only to die. Instead of expiring, the entity glows incandescent magenta and condenses into an egg-like vessel.

The cosmic egg departs into deep space, transforming across metaphysical planes into a psychedelic, kaleidoscopic eye. Back on Earth, the traumatized commuter is found unconscious on the sidewalk by passersby.

Camera style: Pixel-art animated 2D perspective shifts with scrolling side-view walks and flat graphic compositions.

shows.name: Cock Kung-Fu: The Legend of Noemotion
shows.synopsis:
Across an eccentric metropolis, reports circulate concerning the deceitful practices of Dr. Chasity, a rogue medical practitioner operating a fraudulent clinic. When local residents are deceived and captured, martial arts vigilante Noemotion Goldmask takes action.

Donning his signature yellow tunic and golden theater mask, Noemotion equips his katana and flying rocket cycle. He battles clinic henchmen, mechanical automatons, and bizarre monstrosities across city streets, wilderness jungles, and ancient courtyards to reach the mastermind's inner sanctum.

Inside an ornate cathedral stronghold, Noemotion confronts Dr. Chasity in a duel of martial arts prowess and high-tech weaponry. After defeating the corrupt surgeon, the golden-masked hero frees the captives imprisoned in the villain's cells.

Camera style: Cut-out collage animation resembling 2D side-scroller beat-'em-ups with multiplane compositing and locked theatrical angles.

shows.name: Daydream State
shows.synopsis:
An evocative surrealist anthology following paper cutout archetypes through shifting dream dimensions. Characters stitched from vintage advertising and cinema navigate landscapes of giant flowers, flying cephalopods, and retro-futuristic biodomes.

Across rhythmic cycles of longing and disillusionment, the figures confront the boundary between romantic fantasy and waking consciousness.

Camera style: Stop-motion cutout collage animation with rhythmic zooms, rotating layers, and sliding card transitions.

shows.name: Driftwave Static
shows.synopsis:
Set within a glitched retro-futuristic operating system, Driftwave Static is an experimental sci-fi anthology where rogue broadcast signals bleed together into a hallucinatory stream of late-stage digital consciousness.

Disparate narratives surface amid hypnotic kaleidoscope visuals: an abrasive animated comedian mocks audience sensitivities, while in a corporate tower, a cybernetic whistleblower stages an apocalyptic mutiny against corrupt executives using psychoactive data streams.

Camera style: Symmetrical kaleidoscopic mirroring, first-person perspective, digital glitch screen artifacts

shows.name: Fat guy with cheese
shows.synopsis: A gargantuan, wheezing man lives a solitary existence in a dilapidated apartment where every waking moment is dedicated to the consumption and pursuit of exotic dairy. This biological anomaly navigates a world that finds him repulsive, yet he possesses the uncanny ability to physically transmute into various forms of processed cheese to bypass obstacles. The narrative unfolds through hyper-detailed, nauseating close-ups of melting curds and glistening sweat, punctuated only by guttural grunts and the squelch of grease. As his obsession escalates, the line between man and provolone blurs, leading to surreal, supernatural encounters that defy the laws of physics and biology.

shows.name: FEVER DREAM
shows.synopsis: A nameless, haggard man wanders alone through the vast, decaying architecture of his own comatose mind, driven by a single desperate obsession: find the edge of the dream and wake up. The world he traverses is a non-Euclidean nightmare of melting checkerboard deserts, fleshy spiraling forests, and crumbling organic monuments, rendered in a visceral 90s dark-surrealist aesthetic of sepia, ochre, and bruised purple. His only company comes in the form of the Figments — grotesque, anatomically unstable creatures born from his deepest fears, forgotten regrets, and physical anguish — each one a distorted mirror of his own fractured psyche. To move forward, he cannot fight these manifestations; he must confront, recognize, and accept the broken pieces of himself they represent, dissolving them back into the neon-and-sepia sludge from which they came. It is a profoundly lonely meditation on isolation, the terrifying vastness of the human mind, and the brutal, exhausting act of simply enduring.

shows.name: House party
shows.synopsis: *House Party* is an unhinged, surreal comedy procedural following a bizarre, ragtag crew of club-hoppers who just can't stop stumbling into cosmic crime scenes. Forget the rusty van and the old men in rubber masks—this squad investigates genuine, reality-bending mysteries across a corrupted Showrunner universe. They don’t look for clues in abandoned theme parks; they shake down glitch-demons, biomechanical entities, and shady club promoters right on the dancefloor. It’s a hazy, retro-futuristic trip where solving the case is just the side hustle to keeping the House Party alive.

shows.synopsis:
Drawn to a hidden island fortress beyond ordinary perception, an unorthodox warrior confronts spectral masters of ancient combat disciplines. Navigating shifting color planes and psychological illusions, he undergoes rigorous spiritual trials disguised as rhythmic combat.

To transcend physical limitation and escape the fortress, he must embrace the philosophy of fighting without fighting, shattering illusory foes while mastering his own inner voice amidst surreal dimensional rifts.

Camera style: Experimental video art capture featuring inverted solarized color palettes, video feedback loops, and floating spatial perspectives.

shows.name: Let the Fire Burn
shows.synopsis:
In a scorched realm beset by uncontrollable brushfires, a masked figure emerges as both chronicler and instigator of relentless flames. Superimposed above burning hillsides, rural ranch fences, and residential neighborhoods, the harbinger conducts rituals melting cultural artifacts and toys with handheld torches.

As emergency crews, fire engines, and helicopters battle spreading blazes, the entity declares the inevitability of the inferno. Through rhythmic chants, the figure warns onlookers that indifference to destruction ensures total immolation.

Camera style: Layered digital composite footage merging broadcast disaster documentary video with macro object destruction and chromakeyed front-facing performance.

shows.synopsis:
Set in a decaying digital subconscious, the narrative unfolds across distorted audiovisual transmissions where underground street narratives collide with philosophical meditations on paranoia and reality. The protagonist journeys through fragmented memories, musical expressions, and abstract psychological spaces that blur identity.

As surveillance, paranoia, and existential dread intensify, archival educational broadcasts bleed into gritty street scenes. The central figures attempt to anchor themselves amid sensory overload, moving through rhythmic urban landscapes and kaleidoscopic visual corridors.

Camera style: Heavily processed analog VHS, datamoshed screen captures, solarized thermal-like digital filters, and rapid montage cuts.

shows.name: Recursive Metropolis
shows.synopsis:
An algorithmic megalopolis expands beyond physical limits, duplicating skyscrapers, multi-tier highways, and housing complexes into dizzying mathematical fractals. The city functions as a self-generating ecosystem where natural and mechanical elements blur into synchronized patterns.

Within this monolithic superstructure, solitary humans travel along mechanical paths, trapped in perpetual transit. As the infrastructure folds inward into bottomless vortexes, the boundary between urban architecture, digital simulation, and physical reality completely dissolves.

Camera style: Overhead top-down perspective, kaleidoscopic optical mirroring, recursive infinite zooms, and slit-scan motion blur.

In a media landscape revolutionized by machine intelligence, passive entertainment gives way to interactive world simulation. Creators establish story worlds, while viewers cast themselves into roles, diverge plotlines, and generate new episodic content.

As the boundaries between audience and production dissolve, a decentralized creative ecosystem emerges where collaborative communities build expansive multimedia franchises across animation, live action, and speculative fiction.

Camera style: Documentary-style direct-to-camera interviews intercut with cinematic genre sequences and interface capture.

shows.name: Smoker's Cough: Dimensions in Datamosh
shows.synopsis:
Across fractured planes of reality, distorted travelers journey through surreal landscapes, retro-futuristic transit terminals, and celestial cities. Grounded by a manic explorer driving through glitching desert highways, each dimension presents surreal encounters ranging from cybernetic street dealers to celestial courtrooms.

As reality continually slips and remolds itself through datamoshed digital feedback, the characters must find coherence amidst psychedelic visions, alien transformations, and cryptic bureaucratic checkpoints.

Camera style: Experimental datamoshing, collage animation, and heavy compression glitch transitions.

shows.synopsis:
In an ancient era, the cosmos is turned manually by Father Time upon a grand planetary carousel, serenaded by celestial figures. Below on Earth, mortal travelers struggle against harsh desert conditions when mechanical transportation lacks proper maintenance and oil.

After a stranded motorist perishes in the desert wasteland, celestial intervention in the form of restorative oil drops rains down from the heavens. The fluid resurrects the fallen explorer into a sleek, articulated modern automaton.

Now adapted to the machine age, the automaton navigates high-speed roadways and industrial engines, taking over the operation of the planet's rotating machinery to usher in a frictionless, mechanized future.

Camera style: Stop-motion puppet animation staging with miniature tabletop tracking, locked-off diorama compositions, and optical dissolves.
